video_title: Could You Buy the Knicks Soon? Kind of.

quotes.speaker: Brandon Ross
quotes.summary_phrase: MSG Sports plans to spin off the Knicks and Rangers
quotes.excerpt: MSG Sports, the owners of the Knicks and the Rangers, said they are planning to spin off

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
text_blocks.text: Earlier this year, I am going to do the quick TLDR, MSG Sports, the owners of the Knicks and the Rangers, said they are planning to spin off those two teams into separate companies. You are a guy who follows MSG closely, you know how finance works. What exactly does that mean?

text_blocks.speaker: Brandon Ross
text_blocks.text: It means exactly what you said. The Knicks and Rangers are both part of the same entity right now called MSG Sports, ticker MSGS, and the board has now approved for them to break up into two companies. So you will theoretically have two publicly traded companies, one for the Knicks and one for the Rangers.

quotes.speaker: Brandon Ross
quotes.summary_phrase: Spinning off teams is a strategy to unlock value
quotes.excerpt: There is a spin-off happening now to unlock value and to finance things separately
quotes.quote: It used to all be one company called Cablevision. Throughout the years, you are seeing that there is a spin-off happening now to unlock value and to finance things separately, get different investor groups involved that want pure plays. They have done a series of spins. MSG was spun out of Cablevision. It had MSG Entertainment in it and MSG Sports. MSG Entertainment, the ticker, is the New York venues essentially. The sports teams were broken apart from there to trade on their own for people who just wanted to invest in sports.

quotes.speaker: Brandon Ross
quotes.summary_phrase: Tax law 162(m) affects player salary deductions for public companies
quotes.excerpt: There is a new tax law called 162(m). The five highest paid players on your sports teams
quotes.quote: There is a new tax law called 162(m). What that tax law says is if you are a public company, the five highest paid players on your sports teams, their salaries cannot be deducted for tax purposes. This goes into effect in the 2027-2028 season. You are essentially going to pay an additional 35 million in taxes per year for just the Knicks piece, maybe for the Rangers another 10 million. Together as separate companies, an additional 45 to 50 million dollars in taxes if you are a public company.

quotes.speaker: Brandon Ross
quotes.summary_phrase: Going private could help teams avoid tax penalties
quotes.excerpt: This gives me the option to take the Knicks or the Rangers private at some point
quotes.quote: This gives me the option to take the Knicks or the Rangers private at some point to avoid these taxes on public company. Because remember, the Knicks and the Rangers, they don't make, this year obviously it is going to be a bonanza, they are going to wind up making tens of millions of dollars per home game for the finals and this run and everything else. It is going to be a very profitable year for MSG Sports. But generally, they ride around break-even, and if you lose 30, 40, 50 million dollars on taxes, then your free cash flow is negative.

quotes.speaker: Brandon Ross
quotes.summary_phrase: Breaking up teams maximizes shareholder value
quotes.excerpt: Breaking them apart is going to maximize the valuation that shareholders get if they go private
quotes.quote: Breaking them apart is going to maximize the valuation that shareholders get if they go private by doing it separately. It maximizes the value that shareholders get if they go private.

quotes.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
quotes.summary_phrase: Valuation gap between public and private sports ownership
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks are valued at 9.2 billion dollars, but the market value is 13.5 billion

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Vorkunov
text_blocks.text: The thing that comes to mind for me is this seems like a good way for Jim Dolan and everyone who owns an ownership stake in the private Knicks and Rangers to get paid. Because right now their market cap is like 9.2 billion dollars. Our friends at Sportico, who did not catch trades like Forbes, value those two teams combined at 13.5 billion dollars. That is about 4.3 billion dollars to be made there if you buy out all the public shares and then you go private and start selling minority stakes away.

text_blocks.speaker: Brandon Ross
text_blocks.text: Yeah, 13 or 14, they are writing the same ballpark.

quotes.speaker: Brandon Ross
quotes.summary_phrase: Stock price is rising in anticipation of going private
quotes.excerpt: You have seen the stock go on this huge run to start to catch up
quotes.quote: In anticipation of this, you have seen the stock since you first reached out to me, or read what I wrote, you have seen the stock go on this huge run to start to catch up to what that private market value is. And now the discount is still big, it is still 30 percent, but it is a lot better than it was.

quotes.speaker: Brandon Ross
quotes.summary_phrase: Dolan family maintains voting control over the teams
quotes.excerpt: The Dolan family has the vote, like ultimately controls the vote on this
quotes.quote: Don't forget though, the Dolan family has the vote, like ultimately controls the vote on this. And Jim controls the vote on the Dolan family too.

quotes.speaker: Brandon Ross
quotes.summary_phrase: The Sphere is Jim Dolan's legacy project
quotes.excerpt: It does seem that ultimately, his baby right now, like his legacy, is Sphere
quotes.quote: It does seem that ultimately, his baby right now, like his legacy, is Sphere. That is the thing he invented that is actually has a chance to really change the live music business.

quotes.speaker: Brandon Ross
quotes.summary_phrase: Spin-offs are a standard strategy for unlocking value
quotes.excerpt: This is their MO. Spin to unlock value, spin to unlock value
quotes.quote: Again, this is a company who has done a number of spins in the past. This is their MO. Spin to unlock value, spin to unlock value. And so I think they are also running out of things to spin, so now you are breaking up the Knicks and the Rangers. I don't know what is going to be next.
